   144	The following lemma elucidates structural properties of $\ell$-level CL
   145	functions.
   146	Recall that using our shorthand notation, $x^{L_{<k}}$ and $x^{L_k}$ in the
   147	lemma denote $L_{<k}(x)$ and $L_{k,u}(x^{V_{k,\, u}})$ where $u = L_{<k}(x)$.
   148	
   149	
   150	\begin{lemma}
   151	  \label{lem:cl-kth}
   152		Let $\ell \geq 1$ and $V = \F^n$ for some integer $n \geq 0$.
   153	  A function $L: V \to V$ is an $\ell$-level CL function if and only if the
   154	  following collection of functions and subspaces exists:
   155	  \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
   156	  \item \label{enu:cl-k-marginal} For each $k \in \{1, 2, \ldots, \ell\}$, a
   157	    function $L_{\le k} : V \to V$ called the \emph{$k$-th marginal of $L$};
   158	  \item \label{enu:cl-k-space} For each $k \in \{1, 2, \ldots, \ell\}$ and $u
   159	    \in L_{<k} (V)$, a register subspace $V_{k,\, u}$ of $V$ called the
   160	    \emph{$k$-th factor space with prefix $u$};
   161	  \item \label{enu:cl-k-map} For each $k \in \{1, 2, \ldots, \ell\}$ and $u \in
   162	    L_{<k} (V)$, a linear map $L_{k,\, u} : V_{k,\, u} \to V_{k,\, u}$ called
   163	    the \emph{$k$-th linear map of $L$ with prefix $u$};
   164	  \end{enumerate}
   165	  such that the following conditions hold for all $k \in \{1, 2, \ldots,
   166	  \ell\}$.
   167	  \begin{enumerate}
   168	  \item \label{enu:cl-k-cl} $L_{\leq k}$ is a $k$-level CL function on $V$;
   169		\item \label{enu:cl-space-sum} $V = \bigoplus_{i = 1}^\ell V_{i,\,
   170	      x^{L_{<i}}}$ for all $x \in V$;
   171	\item \label{enu:cl-map-sum} $L_{\leq k}(x) = \sum_{i = 1}^{k} x^{L_i}$ for
   172	    all $x \in V$, where $L_i$ is shorthand notation for $L_{i,\,
   173	      x^{L_{<i}}}$;
   174	  \item \label{enu:cl-last-ell} $L = L_{\leq \ell}$.
   175	  \end{enumerate}
   176	  As in \cref{enu:cl-map-sum}, we sometimes use $V_k$ and $L_k$ to denote
   177	  $V_{k,\, u}$ and $L_{k,\, u}$ respectively, leaving the prefix $u$ implicit.
   178	\end{lemma}
   179	
   180	\begin{proof}
   181		We first prove the ``if'' direction: if there exist spaces and functions
   182	  satisfying the conditions in the lemma, the fact that $L$ is an $\ell$-level
   183	  CL function follows from \cref{enu:cl-k-cl,enu:cl-last-ell} of the lemma
   184	  statement.
   185	
   186	  We now prove the ``only if'' direction.
   187	  Given a CL function $L$ on $V$, we construct the $k$-th family of subspaces
   188	  and functions for all $k \in \{1, \ldots, \ell\}$ by induction on the level
   189	  $\ell$.
   190	  First consider the base case $\ell=1$.
   191	  Since $L_{<1} = 0$, we omit the mentioning of the prefix $u \in L_{<1}(V)$.
   192	  Define $L_{\leq 1} = L$, the factor space $V_1 = V$, and the linear map $L_1 =
   193	  L$.
   194	  It is straightforward to verify that the conditions in the lemma hold for
   195	  these choices of linear maps and spaces.
   196	  
   197	  Now, assume that the lemma holds for CL functions of level at most $\ell - 1$,
   198	  and we prove the lemma for $\ell$-level CL functions.
   199	  By definition, an $\ell$-level CL function $L$ can be written as
   200	  \begin{equation*}
   201	  	L(x) = x^{L_1} + L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}(x^{V_{>1}})
   202	  \end{equation*}
   203	  for some linear map $L_1 : V_1 \to V_1$ and a family of $(\ell-1)$-level CL
   204	  functions
   205	  \begin{equation*}
   206	    \bigl \{ L_{>1,\, v} : V_{>1} \to V_{>1} \bigr \}_{\, v \in L_1(V_1)}
   207	  \end{equation*}
   208	  where $V_1$ and $V_{>1}$ are complementary register subspaces of $V$.
   209	  Next, using the inductive hypothesis on the $(\ell-1)$-level CL function
   210	  $L_{>1,\, v}$ we get that for all $v \in L_1(V_1)$ and all $k \in \{1, 2,
   211	  \ldots, \ell-1\}$ there exist $k$-th marginal functions $L'_{v,\, \le k}:
   212	  V_{>1} \to V_{>1}$, $k$-th factor spaces $V'_{v,\, k,\, u}$, and $k$-th linear
   213	  maps $L'_{v,\, k,\, u}$ of $L_{>1,\, v}$ with prefix $u \in L'_{v,\,
   214	    <k}(V_{>1})$ such that the conditions of the lemma for $L_{>1,\, v}$ hold.
   215	  
   216	  Define the marginal functions $L_{\le k} : V \to V$, factor spaces
   217	  $V_{k,\, u}$ and linear maps $L_{k,\, u}$ for $L$ as follows.
   218	  \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
   219	  \item Define $L_{\le 1} = L_1$ and the first factor space to be $V_1$;
   220	  \item For all $k \in \{2, 3, \ldots, \ell\}$, define
   221	    \begin{equation}
   222	      \label{eq:cl-k-def}
   223	      L_{\le k}: x \mapsto x^{L_1} + L'_{x^{L_1},\, <k} (x^{V_{>1}})
   224	      \quad\text{for } x\in V;
   225	    \end{equation}
   226		\item For all $k \in \{2, 3, \ldots, \ell\}$ and $u \in L_{< k}(V)$, define
   227	    $V_{k,\, u} = V'_{v,\, k-1,\, w}$ and $L_{k,\, u} = L'_{v,\, k-1,\, w}$
   228	    where $v = u^{V_1} \in L_{1}(V_{1})$ and $w = u^{V_{>1}} \in L'_{v,< k-1}(V_{> 1})$.
   229	  \end{enumerate}
   230	  We verify that the conditions of the lemma are satisfied.
   231	  Since $L'_{v,\, < k}$ is by assumption a $(k-1)$-level CL function on $V_{>
   232	    1}$, we get that $L_{\leq k}$ is a $k$-level CL function on $V$ from
   233	  \cref{eq:cl-k-def}, establishing \cref{enu:cl-k-cl}.
   234	  By the induction hypothesis, we have for all $v\in L_1(V_1)$ and $y \in
   235	  V_{>1}$,
   236	  \begin{equation}
   237	    \label{eq:cl-k-1}
   238	    V_{>1} = \bigoplus_{i=1}^{\ell-1}
   239	    V'_{\smash{v,\, i, \, y^{L'_{v,\, <i}}}},
   240	  \end{equation}
   241	  which implies that for all $x \in V$ and $v = x^{L_1}$,
   242	  \begin{equation*}
   243	    V = V_1 \oplus \Big ( \bigoplus_{i=1}^{\ell-1}
   244	    V'_{\smash{v,\, i, \, x^{L'_{v,\, <i}}}} \Big)
   245	    = V_1 \oplus \Big (\bigoplus_{i=2}^{\ell} V_{i,\, x^{L_{<i}}} \Big)
   246	    = \bigoplus_{i=1}^\ell V_{i,\, x^{L_{<i}}}\;.
   247	  \end{equation*}
   248	  The first equality follows from \cref{eq:cl-k-1} while the second and third
   249	  equalities follow from the definition of $V_{k,\, u}$.
   250	  This establishes \cref{enu:cl-space-sum}.
   251	
   252	  Next, we have that for all $x \in V$, $v = x^{L_1}$, and $k \in
   253	  \{1,2,\ldots,\ell\}$,
   254	  \begin{align}
   255	    \label{eq:cl-last-ell}
   256	    L_{\leq k}(x)
   257	    & = v + L'_{v,\, <k} (x^{V_{>1}}) \\
   258	    & = v + \sum_{i=1}^{k-1} x^{L'_{v,\, i}}
   259	    = \sum_{i = 1}^{k} x^{L_{i}}, \label{eq:cl-last-ell2}
   260	  \end{align}
   261	  where $L'_{v,\, i}$ is the $i$-th linear map of $L_{>1,\, v}$ with prefix
   262	  $L'_{v,\, <i}(x)$ and $L_i$ is the $i$-th linear map of $L$ with prefix
   263	  $L_{<i}(x)$.
   264	  The second equality follows from the inductive hypothesis applied to $L'_{v,\,
   265	    <k}$ and the third equality follows from the definition of $L_{i}$.
   266	  Line~\eqref{eq:cl-last-ell2} implies \cref{enu:cl-map-sum} of the lemma.
   267	  
   268	  Finally, \Cref{enu:cl-last-ell} follows from~\eqref{eq:cl-last-ell} where we
   269	  set $k = \ell$ and observe that $L'_{x^{L_1},\, \le \ell-1}$ is equal to
   270	  $L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$ by the inductive hypothesis.
   271	  This shows that $L_{\le k}$, $V_{k,\, u}$, and $L_{k,\, u}$ satisfy the
   272	  conditions of the lemma and completes the induction.
   273	\end{proof}
   274	
   275	We note that the marginal functions, factor spaces, and linear maps of a given
   276	CL function $L$ may not be unique; for example, consider the identity function
   277	on a linear space $V = \F^n$.
   278	This is clearly a $1$-level CL function, but it can also be viewed as a
   279	$k$-level CL function for $k \in \{2, \ldots, n\}$ with an arbitrary partition
   280	of $V$ into factor spaces.
   281	
   282	\begin{lemma}
   283	  \label{lem:cl-concat}
   284	  Let $\ell, k \ge 0$ be integers and $U = \F^n$, $V = \F^m$ be linear spaces.
   285	  Suppose $L$ is a $k$-level CL function on $U$ and $R_u$ is an $\ell$-level CL
   286	  function on $V$ for each $u \in L(U)$.
   287	  Then the \emph{concatenation} $T$ of $L$ and $\{R_u\}_u$ defined as
   288	  \begin{equation*}
   289	    T (x) = L(x^U) + R_{L(x^U)} (x^V)
   290	  \end{equation*}
   291	  is a $(k+\ell)$-level conditionally linear function on $U\oplus V$.
   292	\end{lemma}
   293	
   294	\begin{proof}
   295	  We prove the claim by induction on $k$.
   296	  The case $k = 0$ follows from the Definition~\ref{def:cl-func}.
   297	  Assume that the lemma holds for $L$ being at most $(k-1)$-level.
   298	  By Definition~\ref{def:cl-func}, there are complementary register subspaces
   299	  $U_1$ and $U_{>1}$ of $U$, a linear function $L_1$ on $U_1$, and a family of
   300	  $(k-1)$-level CL functions $L_{>1,\, v}$ for $v \in L_1(U_1)$ such that
   301	  \begin{equation*}
   302	    L(x^U) = x^{L_1} + L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}(x^{U_{>1}}).
   303	  \end{equation*}
   304	  For all $x^{L_1}$, define the function $T_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$ on $U_{>1} \oplus V$ as
   305	  \begin{equation*}
   306	    T_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}(x^{U_{>1} \oplus V}) = L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}(x^{U_{>1}}) +
   307	    R_{x^{L_1} + x^{L_{>1}}}(x^V),
   308	  \end{equation*}
   309	  the concatenation of $L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$ and $\{ R_{L(x^U)} \}_{x^{L_{>1}}}$
   310	  where $L_{>1}$ is the shorthand notation of $L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$.
   311	  By the induction hypothesis, $T_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$ is $(k+\ell-1)$-level
   312	  conditionally linear.
   313	  The lemma follows from Definition~\ref{def:cl-func}.
   314	\end{proof}
   315	\begin{lemma}[Direct sums of CL functions]
   316	  \label{lem:cl-func-prod}
   317	  Let $V^{(1)}, V^{(2)}, \ldots, V^{(m)}$ be register subspaces of $V$ such that
   318	  $V = \bigoplus_{j=1}^m V^{(j)}$.
   319	  Suppose that, for each $j\in\{1, 2, \ldots, m\}$, $L^{(j)}$ is an
   320	  $\ell_j$-level conditionally linear function on $V^{(j)}$.
   321	  Then the direct sum $L = \bigoplus_{j=1}^m L^{(j)}$ is an $\ell$-level CL
   322	  function over $V$ for $\ell = \max_j \{\ell_j\}$, where $L$ is defined by
   323	  \begin{equation*}
   324	    L(x) = \sum_{j=1}^m  L^{(j)}(x^{(j)})
   325	  \end{equation*}
   326	  for all $x = \sum_{j=1}^m x^{(j)} \in \bigoplus_{j=1}^m V^{(j)}$.
   327	\end{lemma}
   328	
   329	\begin{proof}
   330	  It is easy to see that an $\ell$-level CL function is also $k$-level
   331	  conditionally linear for all $k \ge \ell$.
   332	  Hence, it suffices to prove the claim where $\ell_j = \ell$ for $j=1, 2,
   333	  \ldots, m$.
   334	
   335	  We prove the theorem by an induction on $\ell$.
   336	  For $\ell = 1$, the functions $L^{(j)}$ are linear and the claim follows by
   337	  the fact that the direct sum of linear maps is linear.
   338	
   339	  Assume now the theorem holds for conditionally linear functions of level at
   340	  most $\ell-1$ and $L^{(j)}$ are $\ell$-level conditionally linear functions
   341	  for $j=1, 2, ,\ldots, m$.
   342	  By definition, $L^{(j)}$ is the concatenation of conditionally linear
   343	  functions $L^{(j)}_{1}$ on $V^{(j)}_1$ and $\{ L^{(j)}_{>1,\, v_j} \}_{v_j}$
   344	  on $V^{(j)}_{>1}$ of levels $1$, and $\ell-1$ respectively.
   345	  Furthermore,
   346	  \begin{equation*}
   347	    L(x) = \sum_{j=1}^m L^{(j)} (x^{(j)}) = \sum_{j=1}^m \Bigl( v_j +
   348	    L^{(j)}_{>1,\, v_j}
   349	    \Bigl((x^{(j)})^{V^{(j)}_{>1}} \Bigr) \Bigr),
   350	  \end{equation*}
   351	  where $v_j = L^{(j)}_{1}\Bigl( (x^{(j)})^{V^{(j)}_1}
   352	    \Bigr)$.
   353	  By the induction hypothesis,
   354	  \begin{equation*}
   355	    L_{1} (x^{V_1}) = \sum_{j=1}^m L^{(j)}_{1}\Bigl( (x^{(j)})^{V^{(j)}_1}
   356	    \Bigr),\quad L_{>1,\, v} (x^{V_{>1}}) = \sum_{j=1}^m L^{(j)}_{>1,\, v_j}
   357	    \Bigl((x^{(j)})^{V^{(j)}_{>1}} \Bigr)
   358	  \end{equation*}
   359	  are $1$-level and $(\ell-1)$-level conditionally linear respectively for $v =
   360	  \sum_j v_j$, $V_1 = \bigoplus_{j=1}^m V^{(j)}_1$, and $V_{>1} =
   361	  \bigoplus_{j=1}^m V^{(j)}_{>1}$.
   362	  This proves that $L$ is $\ell$-level conditionally linear.
   363	\end{proof}
   364	
   365	\begin{lemma}
   366	  \label{lem:cl-dist-prod}
   367	  For each $i \in \{1,\ldots,m\}$ let $L^{(i)}, R^{(i)} : V^{(i)} \to V^{(i)}$
   368	  be $\ell_i$-level conditionally linear functions and let $L, R: V \to V$ be the
   369	  direct sums $L = \bigoplus_i L_i$ and $R = \bigoplus_i R_i$, respectively, as
   370	  defined in Lemma~\ref{lem:cl-func-prod}.
   371	  Then the conditionally linear distribution $\mu_{L, R}$ is the product
   372	  distribution $\prod_{i=1}^m \mu_{L^{(i)},\, R^{(i)}}$ over $V \times V$.
   373	\end{lemma}
   374	
   375	\begin{proof}
   376		The distribution $\mu_{L,R}$ is the distribution over pairs $(L(x),R(x))$
   377	  where $x$ is sampled uniformly from $V \times V$.
   378	  By Lemma~\ref{lem:cl-func-prod}, this is equivalent to the distribution over
   379	  pairs $\bigl( (L_i(x^{V_i}))_{i=1}^m, (R_i(x^{V_i}))_{i=1}^m \bigr)$ where $x$
   380	  is chosen uniformly at random from $V$.
   381	  This distribution is exactly the product of the distributions $

    33	auxiliary for `lem:cl-dist-prod`, blueprint `lem:cl-supported-vanishing`. -/
    34	theorem CondLinearTerm.eval_eq_zero_of_not_mem {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
    35	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {ell : ℕ}
    36	    {t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell} {S : Finset ι}
    37	    (ht : CondLinearTerm.supportedOn t S) (x : ι → K) {a : ι} (ha : a ∉ S) :
    38	    CondLinearTerm.eval t x a = 0 := by
    39	  induction t generalizing S with
    40	  | zero => rfl
    41	  | @succ ell S₁ L₁ hSupport rest ih =>
    42	      rcases ht with ⟨hS₁, hrest⟩
    43	      change (L₁ (coordinateRestriction S₁ x) +
    44	        CondLinearTerm.eval (rest (L₁ (coordinateRestriction S₁ x))) x) a = 0
    45	      rw [Pi.add_apply, hSupport _ a (fun haS₁ => ha (hS₁ haS₁))]
    46	      rw [ih _ (hrest _) (fun haDiff => ha (Finset.mem_sdiff.mp haDiff).1)]
    47	      exact zero_add 0

    50	on the coordinates in its register. -/
    51	private theorem CondLinearTerm.eval_congr_of_eq_on {K ι : Type*} [Field K]

    53	    {t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell} {S : Finset ι}
    54	    (ht : CondLinearTerm.supportedOn t S) {x y : ι → K}
    55	    (hxy : ∀ a ∈ S, x a = y a) :
    56	    CondLinearTerm.eval t x = CondLinearTerm.eval t y := by
    57	  induction t generalizing S with
    58	  | zero => rfl
    59	  | @succ ell S₁ L₁ hSupport rest ih =>
    60	      rcases ht with ⟨hS₁, hrest⟩
    61	      have hrestrict : coordinateRestriction S₁ x = coordinateRestriction S₁ y := by
    62	        ext a
    63	        by_cases ha : a ∈ S₁
    64	        · simp [coordinateRestriction, ha, hxy a (hS₁ ha)]
    65	        · simp [coordinateRestriction, ha]
    66	      simp only [CondLinearTerm.eval, hrestrict]
    67	      rw [ih _ (hrest _) (fun a ha => hxy a (Finset.mem_sdiff.mp ha).1)]

    86	    [DecidableEq ι] {S T : Finset ι} (hST : S ⊆ T) (x : ι → K) :
    87	    coordinateRestriction S (coordinateRestriction T x) = coordinateRestriction S x := by
    88	  ext a

    97	theorem coordinateRestriction_sum_eq {K ι J : Type*} [Field K]
    98	    [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype J]
    99	    (V : J → Finset ι) (hDisjoint : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → Disjoint (V i) (V j))

   101	    coordinateRestriction (V j) (∑ i, f i) = f j := by

   107	    · intro i _ hij

   109	      intro hai
   110	      exact Finset.disjoint_left.mp (hDisjoint i j hij) hai ha
   111	    · exact fun hj => (hj (Finset.mem_univ j)).elim
   112	  · rw [coordinateRestriction]
   113	    simp [ha, hf j a ha]

   365	/-- Equal-level direct sums of maps on disjoint registers are conditionally
   366	linear on the union of those registers.  This is a formalization-only

   368	`lem:cl-func-prod-same-level`. -/
   369	theorem IsCondLinearOn.directSum_sameLevel {K ι J : Type*} [Field K]
   370	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype J]
   371	    (V : J → Finset ι) (ell : ℕ) (L : J → (ι → K) → (ι → K))
   372	    (hDisjoint : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → Disjoint (V i) (V j))
   373	    (hL : ∀ j, IsCondLinearOn K (V j) ell (L j)) :
   374	    IsCondLinearOn K (Finset.univ.biUnion V) ell
   375	      (fun x => ∑ j, L j (coordinateRestriction (V j) x)) := by
   376	  classical
   377	  choose t ht ht_eval using hL
   378	  refine ⟨CondLinearTerm.directSum V ell t,
   379	    CondLinearTerm.directSum_supportedOn V hDisjoint ell t ht, ?_⟩
   380	  funext x
   381	  rw [CondLinearTerm.eval_directSum V hDisjoint ell t ht x]
   382	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   383	  intro j _
   384	  exact congrFun (ht_eval j) (coordinateRestriction (V j) x)

   658	/-- Every positive-level supported representation of a conditionally linear

   660	private theorem CondLinearTerm.nonempty_clDataOn {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
   661	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {ell : ℕ} (hEll : 1 ≤ ell)
   662	    (t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell) {S : Finset ι}
   663	    (ht : CondLinearTerm.supportedOn t S) :
   664	    Nonempty (CLDataOn K ι S ell (CondLinearTerm.eval t)) := by
   665	  induction ell using Nat.strong_induction_on generalizing S with
   666	  | h ell ih =>
   667	      cases ell with
   668	      | zero => omega
   669	      | succ n =>
   670	          cases n with
   671	          | zero => exact CondLinearTerm.nonempty_clDataOn_one t ht
   672	          | succ n =>
   673	              cases t with
   674	              | @succ ell S₁ L₁ hSupport rest =>
   675	                  apply CondLinearTerm.nonempty_clDataOn_succ S₁ L₁ hSupport rest ht
   676	                  intro y
   677	                  exact ih (n + 1) (by omega) (by omega) (rest y) (ht.2 y)

   710	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1123-1134`, paper
   711	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:315-364`. -/
   712	def condLinearDirectSum {K ι : Type*} [Field K] [DecidableEq ι] {m : ℕ}
   713	    (V : Fin m → Finset ι) (L : Fin m → (ι → K) → (ι → K))
   714	    (x : ι → K) : ι → K :=

   717	/-- Maximum of the levels in a finite direct sum. This formalization-only
   718	auxiliary uses `0` for the empty family; `lem:cl-func-prod` separately assumes
   719	the source boundary `m ≥ 1`. -/
   720	def directSumLevel {m : ℕ} (ell : Fin m → ℕ) : ℕ :=
   721	  Finset.univ.sup ell
   722	
   723	/-- Direct sums over a register partition preserve conditional linearity. The
   724	level-zero case is included explicitly, as required by the local correction to
   725	`lem:cl-func-prod`; blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1123-1134`, paper
   726	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:315-364`. -/
   727	theorem IsCondLinear.directSum {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
   728	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {m : ℕ} (hm : 1 ≤ m)
   729	    (V : Fin m → Finset ι) (ell : Fin m → ℕ)
   730	    (L : Fin m → (ι → K) → (ι → K))
   731	    (hDisjoint : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → Disjoint (V i) (V j))
   732	    (hCover : ∀ a, ∃ i, a ∈ V i)
   733	    (hL : ∀ j, IsCondLinearOn K (V j) (ell j) (L j)) :
   734	    IsCondLinear (directSumLevel ell) (condLinearDirectSum V L) := by
   735	  classical
   736	  let _sourceIndex : Fin m := ⟨0, hm⟩
   737	  have hLevel (j : Fin m) : ell j ≤ directSumLevel ell :=
   738	    Finset.le_sup (f := ell) (Finset.mem_univ j)
   739	  have hRaised (j : Fin m) :
   740	      IsCondLinearOn K (V j) (directSumLevel ell) (L j) :=
   741	    IsCondLinearOn.mono_level (hL j) (hLevel j)
   742	  have hUnion : Finset.univ.biUnion V = (Finset.univ : Finset ι) := by
   743	    apply Finset.eq_univ_of_forall
   744	    intro a
   745	    obtain ⟨j, haj⟩ := hCover a
   746	    exact Finset.mem_biUnion.mpr ⟨j, Finset.mem_univ _, haj⟩
   747	  have hSum := IsCondLinearOn.directSum_sameLevel V (directSumLevel ell) L
   748	    hDisjoint hRaised

178	\paragraph{Question distribution.}
   179	We now present the question distribution of the game $\game^\ld$ as a typed CL
   180	distribution (see \Cref{sec:types} for the definition of typed CL functions and
   181	typed CL distributions).
   182	The type set $\type^\ld$ of the game $\game^\ld$ we use is
   183	\[
   184		\type^\ld = \{ \Point, \ALine, \DLine \}\;.
   185	\]
   186	The distribution over question types is uniform over $\type^\ld \times \type^\ld$. 
   187	
   188	We introduce the corresponding typed CL functions $L_\Point$, $L_\ALine$,
   189	$L_\DLine$ where the corresponding CL distributions $\mu_{L_\ALine,L_\Point}$
   190	and $\mu_{L_\DLine,L_\Point}$ implement the axis line-versus-point and diagonal
   191	line-versus-point distributions, respectively.
   192	The functions are parametrized by a field size $q$, a dimension $m$, and three
   193	complementary register subspaces $V_\xpt,V_{\coord}, V_{\dir{}}$ of some ambient
   194	space.
   195	The register $V_\xpt$ (which is isomorphic to $\F_q^m$) is called the
   196	\emph{point register}, $V_\coord$ (which is isomorphic to $\F_q$) is called the
   197	\emph{coordinate register}, and $V_{\dir{}}$ (which is isomorphic to $\F_q^m$)
   198	is called the \emph{direction register}, respectively.
   199	We let $V$ denote the direct sum $V_\xpt \oplus V_{\coord} \oplus V_{\dir{}}$.
   200	We identify elements of $V$ as triples $(u,s,v) \in \F_q^m \times \F_q \times
   201	\F_q^m$.
   202	
   203	Define $L_\Point$ to be the $1$-level CL function that projects onto $V_\xpt$: for every $(u,s,v) \in V$,
   204	\begin{equation}
   205	  \label{eq:cl-ptf}
   206		L_\Point(u,s,v) = (u,0,0) \;.
   207	\end{equation}
   208	Define $L_\ALine$ to be the following $2$-level CL function:
   209	\begin{equation}
   210	  \label{eq:cl-alnf}
   211		L_\ALine(u,s,v) = (L^\lnf_{e_i}(u), s, 0)\ \text{for all } (u,s,v) \in V,
   212	\end{equation}
   213	where $L^\lnf$ is the linear function used to compute the canonical
   214	representative of lines (see \Cref{def:line-representative}), and $i = \chi(s)$
   215	where we define $\chi(s)$ to be the unique integer such that
   216	\begin{equation}
   217	\label{eq:chi-func}
   218		s = (\chi(s) - 1) \frac{q}{m} + r
   219	\end{equation}
   220	for some $0 \leq r < q/m$, and we interpret the field element $s \in \F_q$ as an
   221	integer between $0$ and $q - 1$).
   222	The function $L_\ALine$ is the concatenation of the $1$-level CL function that
   223	projects the subspaces $V_{\coord} \oplus V_{\dir{}}$ down to $V_\coord$ (i.e.
   224	zeroes out the entire $V_{\dir{}}$ register), and the family of $1$-level CL
   225	functions $\{L^\lnf_{e_i} \}$ acting on $V_\xpt$, indexed by $i \in
   226	\{1,2,\ldots,m\}$.
   227	(See \Cref{lem:cl-concat} for definition of CL function concatenation.)
   228	Thus $L_\ALine$ is a $2$-level CL function.
   229	
   230	Define $L_\DLine$ to be the following $3$-level CL function: for all $(u,s,v) \in
   231	V$,
   232	\begin{equation}
   233	\label{eq:cl-dlnf}
   234		L_\DLine(u,s,v) = (L^\lnf_{\pi_{i-1}(v)}(u),s,\pi_{i-1}(v))
   235	\end{equation}
   236	where $i = \chi(s)$.
   237	The function $L_\DLine$ is the concatenation of the following CL functions (again, see \Cref{lem:cl-concat} for definition of CL function concatenation): (i) the identity function on $V_{\coord}$ (which is a $1$-level CL function); (ii) for every $i \in \{1,2,\ldots,m\}$ the $1$-level CL function on $V_{\dir{}}$ that maps $v \mapsto \pi_{i-1}(v)$ (i.e.~it zeroes out the first $i-1$ coordinates of $v$), and (iii) for every pair $(s,v') \in V_\coord \oplus V_{\dir{}}$, the $1$-level CL function $L^\lnf_{v'}$ acting on $V_\xpt$. Thus $L_\DLine$ is a $3$-level CL function.
   238	
   239	
   240	The following two lemmas establish that the CL functions
   241	$L_\Point,L_\ALine,L_\DLine$ give rise to the axis-parallel line-versus-point and
   242	diagonal line-versus-point distributions.
   243	\begin{lemma}
   244		\label{lem:alnf}
   245		Consider the pair $(\line, u)$ sampled in the following way: first, sample the
   246	  tuple $((u_0,s,0),(u,0,0))$ from the CL distribution $\mu_{L_\ALine,L_\Point}$,
   247	  and let $\line = \line(u_0,e_i)$ where $i = \chi(s)$.
   248	  Then $u$ is a uniformly random point in $\F_q^m$ and $\line$ is a line that
   249	  goes through $u$ and is parallel to a uniformly random axis $i \in
   250	  \{1,2,\ldots,m\}$.
   251	\end{lemma}
   252	\begin{proof}
   253		Since $s$ is uniformly random in $\F_q$ and $m$ divides $q$ by assumption, we
   254	  have that $i$ is uniformly random between $\{1,2,\ldots,m\}$ and therefore
   255	  $(u_0,s)$ specifies a uniformly random axis-parallel line $\line(u_0,e_i)$.
   256	  Since $u_0 = L^{\lnf}_{e_i}(u)$, we have that $u \in \line(u_0,e_i)$.
   257	\end{proof}
   258	
   259	
   260	
   261	\begin{lemma}
   262		\label{lem:dlnf}
   263		Consider the pair $(\line,u)$ sampled in the following way: first, sample the
   264	  tuple $((u_0,s,v),(u,0,0))$ from the CL distribution $\mu_{L_\DLine,L_\Point}$,
   265	  and let $\line = \line(u_0,v)$ where $i = \chi(s)$.
   266	  Then $u$ is a uniformly random point in $\F_q^m$ and $\line$ is a random
   267	  diagonal line that goes through $u$ and shares the first $i-1$ coordinates
   268	  with $u$, for uniformly random $i$.
   269	\end{lemma}
   270	\begin{proof}
   271		The proof of this follows identically to \Cref{lem:alnf}.
   272	\end{proof}

   274	For later convenience we make the following definition. 
   275	
   276	\begin{definition}[Line-point distributions]
   277	        \label{def:line-point-dist}
   278	 The \emph{axis line-point distribution} $D_{\ALine}$ is the
   279	 distribution $\mu_{L_\ALine,L_\Point}$ over pairs $(\ell=(u_0,e_i),u)$
   280	 (we omit the $0$ elements for simplicity). The \emph{diagonal
   281	   line-point distribution} $D_{\DLine}$ is the distribution
   282	 $\mu_{L_\DLine,L_\Point}$  over $(\ell=(u_0,s,v),u)$. The
   283	 \emph{line-point distribution} $D_{\Line}$ is the equal mixture of the axis-parallel line-point distribution and the diagonal line-point distribution.
   284	 In other words, a sample from $D_{\Line}$ is distributed as follows:
   285	 with probability $\tfrac{1}{2}$, output a sample from $D_{\ALine}$,
   286	 and with probability $\tfrac{1}{2}$, output a sample from $D_{\DLine}$.
   287	\end{definition}

   192	
   193	The results of this section are not named in the paper.  They record the

   200	/-- Two finite distributions coincide as soon as their supports and their
   201	weight functions coincide.  Formalization-only extensionality principle for
   202	`Distribution`. -/
   203	theorem Distribution.ext_of_support_of_weight {α : Type*} {μ ν : Distribution α}
   204	    (hsupport : μ.support = ν.support) (hweight : μ.weight = ν.weight) :
   205	    μ = ν := by
   206	  cases μ with
   207	  | mk s w hn ho =>
   208	    cases ν with
   209	    | mk s' w' hn' ho' =>
   210	      have hs : s = s' := hsupport
   211	      have hw : w = w' := hweight
   212	      subst hs
   213	      subst hw
   214	      rfl

   216	/-- Successive push-forwards of a finite distribution compose.
   217	Formalization-only auxiliary for `Distribution.map`. -/
   218	theorem Distribution.map_map {α β γ : Type*}
   219	    [DecidableEq β] [DecidableEq γ]
   220	    (μ : Distribution α) (e : α → β) (f : β → γ) :
   221	    (μ.map e).map f = μ.map fun a => f (e a) := by
   222	  refine Distribution.ext_of_support_of_weight ?_ ?_
   223	  · change (μ.support.image e).image f = μ.support.image fun a => f (e a)
   224	    rw [Finset.image_image]
   225	    rfl
   226	  · funext c
   227	    have hmaps : ∀ a ∈ μ.support.filter fun a => f (e a) = c,
   228	        e a ∈ (μ.support.image e).filter fun b => f b = c := by
   229	      intro a ha
   230	      obtain ⟨ha1, ha2⟩ := Finset.mem_filter.mp ha
   231	      exact Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_image_of_mem _ ha1, ha2⟩
   232	    have hkey := Finset.sum_fiberwise_of_maps_to hmaps μ.weight
   233	    change (∑ b ∈ (μ.support.image e).filter fun b => f b = c,
   234	        ∑ a ∈ μ.support.filter fun a => e a = b, μ.weight a) =
   235	      ∑ a ∈ μ.support.filter fun a => f (e a) = c, μ.weight a

   238	    obtain ⟨-, hb2⟩ := Finset.mem_filter.mp hb
   239	    congr 1
   240	    ext a
   241	    simp only [Finset.mem_filter]
   242	    constructor
   243	    · rintro ⟨ha1, rfl⟩
   244	      exact ⟨⟨ha1, hb2⟩, rfl⟩
   245	    · rintro ⟨⟨ha1, -⟩, hae⟩

     4	/-! # Typed conditionally linear distributions
     5	
     6	Typed question distributions first sample an ordered edge of the type graph and
     7	then sample the corresponding pair of conditionally linear images of one common
     8	uniform seed.
     9	
    10	## References
    11	
    12	These are `def:typed-cl-functions` and `def:typed-cl-distributions` in
    13	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:601-631`, with paper origin
    14	`references/qpbt-paper/07_types.tex:57-94`.
    15	-/
    16	
    17	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    18	
    19	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    20	
    21	/-- A typed family whose member at every type is `ell`-level conditionally
    22	linear. This is `def:typed-cl-functions`, blueprint
    23	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:601-606`, paper
    24	`references/qpbt-paper/07_types.tex:57-63`. -/
    25	def IsTypedCondLinearFamily (K T : Type*) [Field K]
    26	    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    27	    (ell : ℕ) (L : T → (ι → K) → (ι → K)) : Prop :=
    28	  ∀ t, IsCondLinear ell (L t)
    29	
    30	/-- The typed CL distribution: sample a type pair from the graph distribution,
    31	then bind it to the CL distribution selected by those two types. This is
    32	`def:typed-cl-distributions`, blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:626-631`, paper
    33	`references/qpbt-paper/07_types.tex:84-94`. -/
    34	noncomputable def typedCLDistribution {K T ι : Type*}
    35	    [Field K] [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K]
    36	    [Fintype T] [DecidableEq T] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    37	    (E : Finset (Sym2 T)) (hE : E.Nonempty)
    38	    (L R : T → (ι → K) → (ι → K)) :
    39	    Distribution ((T × (ι → K)) × (T × (ι → K))) :=
    40	  Distribution.bind (graphDistribution E hE) fun uv =>
    41	    (clDistribution (L uv.1) (R uv.2)).map fun xy =>
    42	      ((uv.1, xy.1), (uv.2, xy.2))
    43

+private def clReindexLinear {K κ ι : Type*} [Field K] {f : κ → ι}

+      clExtend f (L (fun k => x (f k))) + clExtend f (L (fun k => y (f k)))
+    have h : (fun k => (x + y) (f k)) =
+        (fun k => x (f k)) + (fun k => y (f k)) := rfl
+    rw [h, map_add, clExtend_add hf]

+    show clExtend f (L (fun k => (c • x) (f k))) =

+/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: transport a conditionally linear syntax tree
+along an injective reindexing of registers; see `clExtend`.  Supports

+private def clReindexTerm {K κ ι : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype κ] [DecidableEq κ]
+    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {f : κ → ι} (hf : Function.Injective f) :
+    {ell : ℕ} → CondLinearTerm K (ι := κ) ell → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell
+  | _, .zero => .zero
+  | _, .succ S₁ L₁ h rest =>
+      .succ (S₁.image f) (clReindexLinear hf L₁)
+        (by
+          intro x i hi
+          by_cases hex : ∃ k, f k = i
+          · obtain ⟨k, rfl⟩ := hex
+            have hk : k ∉ S₁ := fun hk => hi (Finset.mem_image_of_mem f hk)
+            show clExtend f (L₁ (fun j => x (f j))) (f k) = 0
+            rw [clExtend_apply hf]

+/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the transported syntax tree is supported on
+any register containing the image of the original support. -/
+private theorem clReindexTerm_supportedOn {K κ ι : Type*} [Field K]
+    [Fintype κ] [DecidableEq κ] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {f : κ → ι}
+    (hf : Function.Injective f) :
+    ∀ {ell : ℕ} (t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := κ) ell) (S : Finset κ)
+      (T : Finset ι), t.supportedOn S → S.image f ⊆ T →
+      (clReindexTerm hf t).supportedOn T := by
+  intro ell t
+  induction t with
+  | zero => intro S T _ _; trivial
+  | succ S₁ L₁ hL rest ih =>
+      intro S T hsupp hST
+      obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := hsupp
+      refine ⟨fun i hi => hST (Finset.image_subset_image h1 hi), fun y => ?_⟩
+      refine ih (fun k => y (f k)) (S \ S₁) (T \ S₁.image f) (h2 _) ?_
+      intro i hi
+      obtain ⟨k, hk, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hi
+      obtain ⟨hkS, hkS₁⟩ := Finset.mem_sdiff.mp hk
+      refine Finset.mem_sdiff.mpr ⟨hST (Finset.mem_image_of_mem f hkS), ?_⟩
+      intro hmem
+      obtain ⟨k', hk', hk'eq⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hmem
+      exact hkS₁ (hf hk'eq ▸ hk')

+private theorem clReindexTerm_eval {K κ ι : Type*} [Field K]

   930	-/

 \section{The Pauli basis test}
 % Paper label sec:qld-game kept for cross-reference fidelity.
 \label{sec:qld-game}
 
 The Pauli basis test is the quantum low individual degree test of Natarajan and Vidick, in the slightly modified form introduced by Natarajan and Wright~\cite{Natarajan2018NEEXP}. Informally, the test certifies that the players share the state $\ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}$, where $M = 2^m$. On a question of type $(\mathsf{Pauli}, W)$ with $W \in \{X,Z\}$, a player is expected to measure the generalized Pauli basis POVM $\{\tau^W_h\}_{h \in \F_q^M}$ of Chapter~\ref{chap:qpbt-algebra} and report the outcome $h$. Most subtests probe limited information about $h$: given a point $u_W \in \F_q^m$, a player is expected to report the evaluation $g_h(u_W)$ of the low-degree encoding $g_h$ of $h$, and for a fixed basis $W$ these probes are checked against each other by the classical low individual degree game of Section~\ref{sec:ld-verifier}. Consistency \emph{between} the two bases is checked through two-outcome probes: given additionally $r_W \in \F_q$, a player reports $\tr(g_h(u_W)\, r_W) \in \F_2$. The two binary measurements obtained in this way for $W = X$ and $W = Z$ either commute or anticommute, according to the value $\gamma \in \F_2$ of Equation~\eqref{eq:gamma-value} below. When $\gamma = 0$ the verifier checks commutation directly by asking for both bits simultaneously; when $\gamma = 1$ the verifier checks anticommutation by playing the Magic Square game, using Theorem~\ref{thm:ms-from-ac}.

+    (hSupport : ∀ x a, a ∉ S₁ → L₁ x a = 0)
+    (d : ∀ y, CLDataOn K ι T (ell + 1) (R y))
+    (hDisjoint : Disjoint S₁ T) (k : Fin (ell + 1)) (x : ι → K) :

+      clDataFirst S₁ L₁ x := by
+  rw [clPrefix_cons_succ, coordinateRestriction_add]

+    factor_subset := ?_

+    refine Fin.cases ?_ (fun i => ?_) k

+    · exact ((d (coordinateRestriction S₁ u)).factor_subset i _).trans
+          Finset.sdiff_subset

+    cases i using Fin.cases with

+        | zero => exact (hij rfl).elim
+        | succ j =>
+            rw [clDataConsFactor_zero]

+    | succ i =>
+        cases j using Fin.cases with
+        | zero =>
+            rw [clDataConsFactor_zero]
+            rw [clDataConsFactor_prefix_succ S₁ L₁ hSupport d hDisjoint]
+            exact (hDisjoint.mono_right
+              ((d (clDataFirst S₁ L₁ x)).factor_subset i _)).symm
+        | succ j =>
+            have hij' : i ≠ j := by
+              intro h
+              subst j
+              exact hij rfl
+            rw [clDataConsFactor_prefix_succ S₁ L₁ hSupport d hDisjoint]
+            rw [clDataConsFactor_prefix_succ S₁ L₁ hSupport d hDisjoint]
+            exact (d (clDataFirst S₁ L₁ x)).factor_disjoint x i j hij'

+    by_cases haS₁ : a ∈ S₁
+    · exact ⟨0, by simpa using haS₁⟩
+    · have haTail : a ∈ S \ S₁ := Finset.mem_sdiff.mpr ⟨ha, haS₁⟩

+        (d (clDataFirst S₁ L₁ x)).factor_cover x a haTail

+      rw [clDataConsFactor_prefix_succ S₁ L₁ hSupport d hDisjoint]
+      exact hai
+  · intro k u x a ha
+    revert ha
+    refine Fin.cases ?_ (fun i => ?_) k
+    · intro ha
+      change L₁ (coordinateRestriction S₁ x) a = 0
+      exact hSupport _ _ ha
+    · intro ha
+      exact (d (coordinateRestriction S₁ u)).linear_supported i
+          (coordinateRestriction (S \ S₁) u) x a ha
+  · intro k x
+    have hhead :
+        clDataConsLinear S₁ L₁ d 0
+            (clPrefix (clDataConsMarginal S₁ L₁ d) 0 x)
+            (coordinateRestriction
+              (clDataConsFactor S₁ d 0
+                (clPrefix (clDataConsMarginal S₁ L₁ d) 0 x)) x) =
+          clDataFirst S₁ L₁ x := by
+      change L₁ (coordinateRestriction S₁ (coordinateRestriction S₁ x)) =
+        L₁ (coordinateRestriction S₁ x)
+      rw [coordinateRestriction_coordinateRestriction Finset.Subset.rfl]
+    refine Fin.cases ?_ (fun j => ?_) k
+    · rw [Fin.sum_univ_succ]
+      simp only [Fin.val_zero, le_refl, ↓reduceIte, hhead]
+      simp
+    · rw [Fin.sum_univ_succ]
+      simp only [Fin.val_zero, Nat.zero_le, ↓reduceIte, hhead]
+      rw [clDataConsMarginal_succ]
+      congr 1
+      rw [(d (clDataFirst S₁ L₁ x)).sum_formula j x]
+      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+      intro i _
+      by_cases hij : i.val ≤ j.val
+      · have hsucc : i.succ.val ≤ j.succ.val := by
+          simpa only [Fin.val_succ, Nat.succ_le_succ_iff] using hij
+        rw [if_pos hsucc, if_pos hij]
+        rw [clDataConsLinear_prefix_succ S₁ L₁ hSupport d hDisjoint]
+        rw [clDataConsFactor_prefix_succ S₁ L₁ hSupport d hDisjoint]
+      · have hsucc : ¬ i.succ.val ≤ j.succ.val := by
+          simpa only [Fin.val_succ, Nat.succ_le_succ_iff] using hij
+        rw [if_neg hsucc, if_neg hij]
+  · intro h
+    have hTail : 0 < ell + 1 := by omega
+    let last : Fin (ell + 1) :=
+      ⟨(ell + 1) - 1, Nat.sub_lt hTail (by decide)⟩
+    have hlast :
+        (⟨((ell + 1) + 1) - 1, Nat.sub_lt h (by decide)⟩ : Fin ((ell + 1) + 1)) =
+          last.succ := by
+      apply Fin.ext
+      simp [last]
+    funext x
+    rw [hlast, clDataConsMarginal_succ]
+    rw [congrFun ((d (clDataFirst S₁ L₁ x)).top hTail) x]
+    rfl

+/-- Every positive-level supported representation of a conditionally linear
+function admits support-relative prefix decomposition data. -/
+private theorem CondLinearTerm.nonempty_clDataOn {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
+    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {ell : ℕ} (hEll : 1 ≤ ell)
+    (t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell) {S : Finset ι}
+    (ht : CondLinearTerm.supportedOn t S) :
+    Nonempty (CLDataOn K ι S ell (CondLinearTerm.eval t)) := by
+  induction ell using Nat.strong_induction_on generalizing S with
+  | h ell ih =>
+      cases ell with
+      | zero => omega
+      | succ n =>
+          cases n with
+          | zero => exact CondLinearTerm.nonempty_clDataOn_one t ht
+          | succ n =>
+              cases t with
+              | @succ ell S₁ L₁ hSupport rest =>
+                  apply CondLinearTerm.nonempty_clDataOn_succ S₁ L₁ hSupport rest ht
+                  intro y
+                  exact ih (n + 1) (by omega) (by omega) (rest y) (ht.2 y)

+import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Games.CondLinear
+
+/-!
+# Coordinate direct sums of conditionally linear representations
+
+This module assembles the direct sum of equal-level representations of
+conditionally linear functions over a family of pairwise disjoint registers,
+together with the coordinate-restriction lemmas its support and evaluation
+proofs rely on.  It is the supporting layer of
+`MIPStarRE/QPBT/Games/CondLinearTheorems.lean`, the module that owns the
+behaviour of conditionally linear maps and of their shared-seed distributions
+under finite coordinate direct sums.
+
+## References
+
+The source result is `lem:cl-func-prod` in
+`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1123-1134`, approached through the
+formalization support nodes `lem:cl-supported-vanishing`,
+`lem:cl-restriction-idem`, `lem:cl-restriction-sum`,
+`lem:cl-supported-restriction`, and `lem:cl-func-prod-same-level` at
+`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1156-1212`.  The paper origin is
+`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:150-379`.
+-/
+
+open scoped BigOperators
+
+namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
+
+open MIPStarRE.LDT
+
+/-- A representation of a conditionally linear function supported on a register
+takes values that vanish off that register.  This is a formalization-only
+auxiliary for `lem:cl-dist-prod`, blueprint `lem:cl-supported-vanishing`. -/
+theorem CondLinearTerm.eval_eq_zero_of_not_mem {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
+    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {ell : ℕ}
+    {t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell} {S : Finset ι}
+    (ht : CondLinearTerm.supportedOn t S) (x : ι → K) {a : ι} (ha : a ∉ S) :
+    CondLinearTerm.eval t x a = 0 := by
+  induction t generalizing S with
+  | zero => rfl
+  | @succ ell S₁ L₁ hSupport rest ih =>
+      rcases ht with ⟨hS₁, hrest⟩
+      change (L₁ (coordinateRestriction S₁ x) +
+        CondLinearTerm.eval (rest (L₁ (coordinateRestriction S₁ x))) x) a = 0
+      rw [Pi.add_apply, hSupport _ a (fun haS₁ => ha (hS₁ haS₁))]
+      rw [ih _ (hrest _) (fun haDiff => ha (Finset.mem_sdiff.mp haDiff).1)]
+      exact zero_add 0
+
+/-- A supported representation of a conditionally linear function depends only
+on the coordinates in its register. -/
+private theorem CondLinearTerm.eval_congr_of_eq_on {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
+    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {ell : ℕ}
+    {t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell} {S : Finset ι}
+    (ht : CondLinearTerm.supportedOn t S) {x y : ι → K}
+    (hxy : ∀ a ∈ S, x a = y a) :
+    CondLinearTerm.eval t x = CondLinearTerm.eval t y := by
+  induction t generalizing S with
+  | zero => rfl
+  | @succ ell S₁ L₁ hSupport rest ih =>
+      rcases ht with ⟨hS₁, hrest⟩
+      have hrestrict : coordinateRestriction S₁ x = coordinateRestriction S₁ y := by
+        ext a
+        by_cases ha : a ∈ S₁
+        · simp [coordinateRestriction, ha, hxy a (hS₁ ha)]
+        · simp [coordinateRestriction, ha]
+      simp only [CondLinearTerm.eval, hrestrict]
+      rw [ih _ (hrest _) (fun a ha => hxy a (Finset.mem_sdiff.mp ha).1)]
+
+/-- Restricting the input to the register supporting a conditionally linear
+function does not change its value.  This is a formalization-only auxiliary
+for `lem:cl-func-prod` and `lem:cl-dist-prod`, blueprint
+`lem:cl-supported-restriction`. -/
+theorem CondLinearTerm.eval_coordinateRestriction {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
+    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {ell : ℕ}
+    {t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell} {S : Finset ι}
+    (ht : CondLinearTerm.supportedOn t S) (x : ι → K) :
+    CondLinearTerm.eval t (coordinateRestriction S x) = CondLinearTerm.eval t x := by
+  exact CondLinearTerm.eval_congr_of_eq_on ht fun a ha => by
+    simp [coordinateRestriction, ha]
+
+/-- Restricting first to a larger register does not affect a subsequent
+restriction to a smaller register.  This is a formalization-only auxiliary
+for `lem:cl-kth` and `lem:cl-func-prod`, blueprint
+`lem:cl-restriction-idem`. -/
+theorem coordinateRestriction_coordinateRestriction {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
+    [DecidableEq ι] {S T : Finset ι} (hST : S ⊆ T) (x : ι → K) :
+    coordinateRestriction S (coordinateRestriction T x) = coordinateRestriction S x := by
+  ext a
+  by_cases ha : a ∈ S
+  · simp [coordinateRestriction, ha, hST ha]
+  · simp [coordinateRestriction, ha]
+
+/-- In a register partition, restricting a sum of supported vectors selects
+the corresponding summand.  This is a formalization-only auxiliary for
+`lem:cl-func-prod` and `lem:cl-dist-prod`, blueprint
+`lem:cl-restriction-sum`. -/
+theorem coordinateRestriction_sum_eq {K ι J : Type*} [Field K]
+    [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype J]
+    (V : J → Finset ι) (hDisjoint : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → Disjoint (V i) (V j))
+    (f : J → ι → K) (hf : ∀ j a, a ∉ V j → f j a = 0) (j : J) :
+    coordinateRestriction (V j) (∑ i, f i) = f j := by
+  ext a
+  by_cases ha : a ∈ V j
+  · rw [coordinateRestriction]
+    simp only [ha, ↓reduceIte, Finset.sum_apply]
+    apply Finset.sum_eq_single j
+    · intro i _ hij
+      apply hf i a
+      intro hai
+      exact Finset.disjoint_left.mp (hDisjoint i j hij) hai ha
+    · exact fun hj => (hj (Finset.mem_univ j)).elim
+  · rw [coordinateRestriction]
+    simp [ha, hf j a ha]
+
+/-- The first register of a positive-level conditionally-linear term. -/
+private def CondLinearTerm.headSupport {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
+    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {ell : ℕ} :
+    CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) (ell + 1) → Finset ι
+  | .succ S₁ _ _ _ => S₁
+
+/-- The first linear map of a positive-level conditionally-linear term. -/
+private def CondLinearTerm.headLinear {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
+    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {ell : ℕ} :
+    CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) (ell + 1) → ((ι → K) →ₗ[K] (ι → K))
+  | .succ _ L₁ _ _ => L₁
+
+/-- The residual family of a positive-level conditionally-linear term. -/
+private def CondLinearTerm.tail {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
+    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {ell : ℕ} :
+    CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) (ell + 1) →
+      ((ι → K) → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell)
+  | .succ _ _ _ rest => rest
+
+private theorem CondLinearTerm.headLinear_eq_zero_of_not_mem
+    {K ι : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {ell : ℕ}
+    (t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) (ell + 1)) (x : ι → K) {a : ι}
+    (ha : a ∉ t.headSupport) : t.headLinear x a = 0 := by
+  cases t with
+  | succ S₁ L₁ hSupport rest => exact hSupport x a ha
+
+private theorem CondLinearTerm.supportedOn_headSupport {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
+    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {ell : ℕ}
+    {t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) (ell + 1)} {S : Finset ι}
+    (ht : CondLinearTerm.supportedOn t S) : t.headSupport ⊆ S := by
+  cases t with
+  | succ S₁ L₁ hSupport rest => exact ht.1
+
+private theorem CondLinearTerm.supportedOn_tail {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
+    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {ell : ℕ}
+    {t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) (ell + 1)} {S : Finset ι}
+    (ht : CondLinearTerm.supportedOn t S) (y : ι → K) :
+    CondLinearTerm.supportedOn (t.tail y) (S \ t.headSupport) := by
+  cases t with
+  | succ S₁ L₁ hSupport rest => exact ht.2 y
+
+private theorem CondLinearTerm.eval_succ_eq {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
+    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {ell : ℕ}
+    (t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) (ell + 1)) (x : ι → K) :
+    CondLinearTerm.eval t x =
+      t.headLinear (coordinateRestriction t.headSupport x) +
+        CondLinearTerm.eval
+          (t.tail (t.headLinear (coordinateRestriction t.headSupport x))) x := by
+  cases t
+  rfl
+
+/-- The sum of the first linear pieces of a finite family of positive-level
+conditionally-linear terms. -/
+private def condLinearHeadSum {K ι J : Type*} [Field K]
+    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J] {ell : ℕ}
+    (t : J → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) (ell + 1)) :
+    (ι → K) →ₗ[K] (ι → K) where
+  toFun x := ∑ j, (t j).headLinear (coordinateRestriction (t j).headSupport x)
+  map_add' x y := by
+    rw [← Finset.sum_add_distrib]
+    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+    intro j _
+    rw [← map_add]
+    congr 1
+    ext b
+    by_cases hb : b ∈ (t j).headSupport <;> simp [coordinateRestriction, hb]
+  map_smul' c x := by
+    rw [Finset.smul_sum]
+    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+    intro j _
+    rw [← map_smul]
+    congr 1
+    ext b
+    by_cases hb : b ∈ (t j).headSupport <;> simp [coordinateRestriction, hb]
+
+/-- Combine equal-level representations of conditionally linear functions on
+disjoint registers. -/
+private def CondLinearTerm.directSum {K ι J : Type*} [Field K]
+    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J]
+    (V : J → Finset ι) :
+    (ell : ℕ) → (J → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell) →
+      CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell
+  | 0, _ => .zero
+  | ell + 1, t =>
+      .succ (Finset.univ.biUnion fun j => (t j).headSupport) (condLinearHeadSum t)
+        (by
+          intro x a ha
+          simp only [condLinearHeadSum, LinearMap.coe_mk, AddHom.coe_mk,
+            Finset.sum_apply]
+          apply Finset.sum_eq_zero
+          intro j _
+          exact CondLinearTerm.headLinear_eq_zero_of_not_mem (t j) _
+            (fun haj => ha (Finset.mem_biUnion.mpr ⟨j, Finset.mem_univ _, haj⟩)))
+        (fun y => directSum (fun j => V j \ (t j).headSupport) ell
+          (fun j => (t j).tail (coordinateRestriction (V j) y)))
+
+private theorem CondLinearTerm.directSum_supportedOn {K ι J : Type*} [Field K]
+    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J]
+    (V : J → Finset ι) (hDisjoint : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → Disjoint (V i) (V j))
+    (ell : ℕ) (t : J → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell)

+  induction ell generalizing V with
+  | zero => trivial
+  | succ ell ih =>
+      have hhead (j : J) : (t j).headSupport ⊆ V j :=
+        CondLinearTerm.supportedOn_headSupport (ht j)

+          (hhead j).trans (Finset.subset_biUnion_of_mem V (Finset.mem_univ j))

+        have hunion :
+            Finset.univ.biUnion (fun j => V j \ (t j).headSupport) =
+              Finset.univ.biUnion V \
+                Finset.univ.biUnion (fun j => (t j).headSupport) := by
+          ext a
+          constructor
+          · intro ha
+            obtain ⟨j, _, hj⟩ := Finset.mem_biUnion.mp ha
+            obtain ⟨haV, haS⟩ := Finset.mem_sdiff.mp hj
+            refine Finset.mem_sdiff.mpr
+              ⟨Finset.mem_biUnion.mpr ⟨j, Finset.mem_univ _, haV⟩, ?_⟩

+private theorem CondLinearTerm.eval_directSum {K ι J : Type*} [Field K]
+    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J]
+    (V : J → Finset ι) (hDisjoint : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → Disjoint (V i) (V j))
+    (ell : ℕ) (t : J → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell)
+    (ht : ∀ j, CondLinearTerm.supportedOn (t j) (V j)) (x : ι → K) :
+    CondLinearTerm.eval (CondLinearTerm.directSum V ell t) x =
+      ∑ j, CondLinearTerm.eval (t j) (coordinateRestriction (V j) x) := by
+  induction ell generalizing V x with
+  | zero =>
+      apply Eq.symm
+      apply Finset.sum_eq_zero
+      intro j _
+      cases t j
+      rfl
+  | succ ell ih =>
+      let S : J → Finset ι := fun j => (t j).headSupport
+      let y : J → ι → K := fun j =>
+        (t j).headLinear (coordinateRestriction (S j) x)
+      have hS (j : J) : S j ⊆ V j :=
+        CondLinearTerm.supportedOn_headSupport (ht j)
+      have hy (j : J) (a : ι) (ha : a ∉ V j) : y j a = 0 := by
+        exact CondLinearTerm.headLinear_eq_zero_of_not_mem (t j) _
+          (fun haS => ha (hS j haS))
+      have hhead :
+          condLinearHeadSum t
+              (coordinateRestriction (Finset.univ.biUnion S) x) = ∑ j, y j := by
+        apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+        intro j _
+        change (t j).headLinear
+            (coordinateRestriction (S j)
+              (coordinateRestriction (Finset.univ.biUnion S) x)) =
+          (t j).headLinear (coordinateRestriction (S j) x)
+        rw [coordinateRestriction_coordinateRestriction
+          (Finset.subset_biUnion_of_mem S (Finset.mem_univ j))]
+      have hselect (j : J) : coordinateRestriction (V j) (∑ i, y i) = y j :=
+        coordinateRestriction_sum_eq V hDisjoint y hy j
+      have htail (j : J) :
+          CondLinearTerm.supportedOn ((t j).tail (y j)) (V j \ S j) := by
+        exact CondLinearTerm.supportedOn_tail (ht j) (y j)
+      have hDisjointTail : ∀ i j, i ≠ j →
+          Disjoint (V i \ S i) (V j \ S j) := by
+        intro i j hij
+        exact (hDisjoint i j hij).mono Finset.sdiff_subset Finset.sdiff_subset
+      have htail_eval (j : J) :
+          CondLinearTerm.eval ((t j).tail (y j))
+              (coordinateRestriction (V j \ S j) x) =
+            CondLinearTerm.eval ((t j).tail (y j))
+              (coordinateRestriction (V j) x) := by
+        have hrestrict := CondLinearTerm.eval_coordinateRestriction
+          (htail j) (coordinateRestriction (V j) x)
+        rwa [coordinateRestriction_coordinateRestriction Finset.sdiff_subset] at hrestrict
+      have hcomponent (j : J) :
+          CondLinearTerm.eval (t j) (coordinateRestriction (V j) x) =
+            y j + CondLinearTerm.eval ((t j).tail (y j))
+              (coordinateRestriction (V j \ S j) x) := by
+        rw [CondLinearTerm.eval_succ_eq]
+        change (t j).headLinear
+              (coordinateRestriction (S j) (coordinateRestriction (V j) x)) +
+            CondLinearTerm.eval
+              ((t j).tail
+                ((t j).headLinear
+                  (coordinateRestriction (S j) (coordinateRestriction (V j) x))))
+              (coordinateRestriction (V j) x) = _
+        rw [coordinateRestriction_coordinateRestriction (hS j)]
+        change y j + CondLinearTerm.eval ((t j).tail (y j))
+            (coordinateRestriction (V j) x) = _
+        rw [htail_eval]
+      have hrec := ih (fun j => V j \ S j) hDisjointTail
+        (fun j => (t j).tail (y j)) htail x
+      have htail_family :
+          (fun j => (t j).tail (coordinateRestriction (V j) (∑ i, y i))) =
+            (fun j => (t j).tail (y j)) := by
+        funext j
+        rw [hselect]
+      calc
+        CondLinearTerm.eval (CondLinearTerm.directSum V (ell + 1) t) x =
+            (∑ j, y j) +
+              CondLinearTerm.eval
+                (CondLinearTerm.directSum (fun j => V j \ S j) ell
+                  (fun j => (t j).tail (y j))) x := by
+              change condLinearHeadSum t
+                    (coordinateRestriction
+                      (Finset.univ.biUnion fun j => (t j).headSupport) x) +
+                  CondLinearTerm.eval
+                    (CondLinearTerm.directSum
+                      (fun j => V j \ (t j).headSupport) ell
+                      (fun j => (t j).tail
+                        (coordinateRestriction (V j)
+                          (condLinearHeadSum t
+                            (coordinateRestriction
+                              (Finset.univ.biUnion fun i => (t i).headSupport) x))))) x = _
+              rw [show (fun j => (t j).headSupport) = S from rfl, hhead]
+              rw [htail_family]
+        _ = (∑ j, y j) + ∑ j, CondLinearTerm.eval ((t j).tail (y j))
+              (coordinateRestriction (V j \ S j) x) := by rw [hrec]
+        _ = ∑ j, (y j + CondLinearTerm.eval ((t j).tail (y j))
+              (coordinateRestriction (V j \ S j) x)) := Finset.sum_add_distrib.symm
+        _ = ∑ j, CondLinearTerm.eval (t j) (coordinateRestriction (V j) x) := by
+              apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+              intro j _
+              exact (hcomponent j).symm
+
+/-- Equal-level direct sums of maps on disjoint registers are conditionally
+linear on the union of those registers.  This is a formalization-only
+auxiliary for `lem:cl-func-prod`, blueprint
+`lem:cl-func-prod-same-level`. -/
+theorem IsCondLinearOn.directSum_sameLevel {K ι J : Type*} [Field K]
+    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype J]
+    (V : J → Finset ι) (ell : ℕ) (L : J → (ι → K) → (ι → K))
+    (hDisjoint : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → Disjoint (V i) (V j))
+    (hL : ∀ j, IsCondLinearOn K (V j) ell (L j)) :
+    IsCondLinearOn K (Finset.univ.biUnion V) ell
+      (fun x => ∑ j, L j (coordinateRestriction (V j) x)) := by
+  classical
+  choose t ht ht_eval using hL
+  refine ⟨CondLinearTerm.directSum V ell t,
+    CondLinearTerm.directSum_supportedOn V hDisjoint ell t ht, ?_⟩
+  funext x
+  rw [CondLinearTerm.eval_directSum V hDisjoint ell t ht x]
+  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+  intro j _
+  exact congrFun (ht_eval j) (coordinateRestriction (V j) x)
+
+end MIPStarRE.QPBT
